design_rationale: This was an individually randomized, two-arm trial with central 1:1 block randomization stratified by country.

domain_judgments.rationale: The centrally administered block-randomized sequence was stratified by country, allocation was concealed in sealed opaque envelopes until after recruitment, and reported baseline characteristics were generally compatible with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Allocation of participants to study groups was done centrally by the trial’s sponsor ... by block randomisation of eight and stratified by country. ... Study number allocation for each study participant was concealed in sealed opaque envelopes that were opened only after recruitment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and trial personnel were masked with identically packaged placebo, treatment was directly observed, co-intervention adherence was similar between groups, and no important intervention-related deviations likely to affect outcomes were evident, although the primary analysis excluded participants without outcome data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Study drug tablets (dihydroartemisinin–piperaquine and placebo) were identically packaged. All study personnel, investigators, outcome assessors, data analysts, and participants remained masked to treatment assignment throughout the trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was available for 602 of 666 randomized participants (90%), with somewhat more missing data in the intervention group (38/332) than placebo group (26/334), and the modified intention-to-treat analysis excluded those missing outcomes without a reported sensitivity analysis establishing robustness to missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Peripheral blood samples were collected at delivery from 602 (90%) of 666 participants, thus contributing to the primary endpoint analysis; of those, 294 women were in the intervention group and 308 women were in the control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: The prespecified primary outcome was objectively measured by standardized, quality-controlled microscopy in both groups, and outcome assessors were masked to assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome of the trial was the prevalence of maternal parasitaemia at delivery defined by the presence of P falciparum asexual parasites of any density in peripheral blood (determined by microscopy).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, its protocol was published, and the primary endpoint and main analysis population were prespecified; post-hoc composite analyses were explicitly identified as such.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03671109. ... Post-hoc analyses (not prespecified in the protocol) were done for (1) malaria infection during study follow-up ... and (2) overall malaria or anaemia at delivery.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by 10% missing primary-outcome data, modest differential missingness between groups, and exclusion of participants without primary-outcome data from the modified intention-to-treat analysis. Randomization, masking, objective outcome measurement, and prespecified reporting were otherwise robust.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports random assignment in a 1:1 ratio using permuted variable-sized blocks of 4 and 6 in a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence used permuted variable-sized blocks and was implemented by pharmacists otherwise uninvolved in the study, supporting random sequence generation and concealment; the modest gravidity imbalance is compatible with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Women were randomly assigned to receive standard chemoprevention with daily TMP-SMX plus monthly placebo or daily TMP-SMX plus monthly DP in a 1:1 ratio, using permuted variable-sized blocks of 4 and 6. Pharmacists not otherwise involved in the study were responsible for treatment allocation and the preparation of study drugs.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and study personnel were blinded with appearance-matched placebo, initial dosing was directly observed, deviations were prespecified for drug interactions, and the modified intention-to-treat analysis excluded only participants without evaluable outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants randomly assigned to receive daily TMP-SMX alone were given DP placebo with the same appearance and number of tablets as active DP.

domain_judgments.rationale: All randomized women were followed through delivery and the primary outcome was available for 194 of 200 (97%), with similarly high retention in both arms (96/100 versus 98/100), making material bias from missingness unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All 200 women enrolled were followed through delivery, and 194 (97%) had placental tissue collected for histopathologic analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was measured identically across groups using standardized placental histopathology, duplicate independent readings, blinded readers, and third-reader resolution of discrepancies.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Slides prepared for histopathologic analysis were read in duplicate, using a standardized case record form, by 2 independent readers (J. A. and G. R.), and any discrepant results were resolved by a third reader (A. M.). Readers were blinded to both treatment assignment and findings of prior reads.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and the primary outcome and analysis are clearly described, but the supplied report does not establish that a prespecified protocol or statistical analysis plan fixed all eligible measurements and analyses before unblinded analysis, and both crude and gravidity-adjusted estimates were available.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Clinical Trials Registration. NCT02282293.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven by incomplete information about prespecification of all outcome analyses and the availability of both crude and gravidity-adjusted estimates. Randomization, blinding, outcome completeness, and blinded standardized outcome measurement were otherwise robust.

design_rationale: This was an individually randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial using centrally generated block randomization stratified by country.

domain_judgments.rationale: The computer-generated, centrally safeguarded block-randomization sequence was concealed in sequentially numbered opaque sealed envelopes, and baseline characteristics were similar between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The Pharmacy Department of the Hospital Clinic in Barcelona produced and safeguarded the computer-generated randomization list for each recruiting site until unblinding... Study number allocation for each participant was concealed in opaque sealed envelopes that were sequentially numbered and opened only after recruitment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and personnel were formally blinded and the main analysis was described as ITT, but conspicuously higher dizziness and vomiting with mefloquine could reveal assignment, and the reported ITT analysis excluded participants without outcome data rather than including every randomized participant.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Investigators, laboratory staff, care providers, and study participants were blinded to intervention throughout the study... The main analysis was done on the Intention-to-Treat (ITT) cohort that included all recruited women that met the inclusion criteria and had data on the specific outcomes.

domain_judgments.rationale: For the primary outcome, data were available for 973 of 1,071 randomized women (90.8%), with nearly identical availability by group (490/537 control and 483/534 mefloquine), making material bias from missingness unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 973 peripheral blood samples from women at delivery were collected (490 from control and 483 from MQ group).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary endpoint was objectively measured using standardized microscopy or PCR applied consistently across groups, with laboratory staff blinded to assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Peripheral malaria infection at delivery (primary study endpoint) was defined as the presence of asexual P. falciparum parasites of any density in a blood smear or filter paper (detected either by optical microscopy or PCR, respectively)... Investigators, laboratory staff, care providers, and study participants were blinded to intervention throughout the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, had an available protocol and statistical analysis plan, and the authors state that all protocol-listed outcomes were reported, substantially limiting selective-reporting concerns for the primary result.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial was registered prior to the enrolment of the first participant... The statistical analysis plan is available in Text S3. Findings of all study outcomes listed in the protocol (Text S1) are reported in the results section and the tables.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by possible functional unblinding from distinctive mefloquine adverse effects and use of a modified ITT population limited to participants with available outcome data. Randomization, objective blinded outcome measurement, balanced and modest primary-outcome missingness, and prospective reporting plans otherwise support low risk.

design_rationale: This was an individually randomized, two-arm trial using a computer-generated permuted-block sequence, with allocation stratified by site and HIV status.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated by an independent statistician, stratified with permuted blocks, and concealed in sequentially numbered, sealed, opaque envelopes; baseline characteristics were well balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An independent statistician not involved in the study generated the randomisation list for the trial pharmacists in Kenya and Malawi, who prepared sequentially numbered, sealed, opaque envelopes for each participant with the randomisation assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, investigators, and analysts were masked with matched placebo; adherence and visit attendance were high, and the modified intention-to-treat analysis excluded only an ineligible participant and participants lacking endpoint data, with sensitivity and per-protocol analyses supporting the result.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All investigators, laboratory staf, data analysts, and participants were masked to treatment assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome data were available for 895 of 904 randomized participants (99%), missingness was balanced between groups, and a non-responder-imputation sensitivity analysis produced similar findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 895 (99%) participants contributed to the primary endpoint analysis... The proportion of eligible participants with missing primary endpoint data was equally distributed across study groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Malaria infection was measured using prespecified objective laboratory and histological methods applied across groups, and all outcome assessors and laboratory staff were masked to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint was the incidence of at least one Plasmodium infection detected in the peripheral (maternal) or placental (maternal) blood or tissue by PCR, microscopy, rapid diagnostic test, or placental histology... All outcome assessors were masked to the treatment groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, its protocol was available, and analyses were prespecified in a statistical analysis plan, with post-hoc analyses explicitly identified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All analyses were prespecified (unless otherwise indicated as post hoc) in a statistical analysis plan approved by the data and safety monitoring board. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04158713.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is low across all five RoB 2 domains. The trial had robust randomization and concealment, comprehensive masking, 99% primary-outcome ascertainment, objective outcome measurement, and prospectively specified analyses.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes two parallel randomized trials, with randomization stratified by study site and gravidity and treatment assignment made centrally by telephone.

domain_judgments.rationale: Central telephone assignment likely concealed allocation and baseline characteristics were similar within each trial, but the method used to generate the random sequence was not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In each trial, randomization was stratified according to the study site and the number of previous pregnancies (primigravid vs. multigravid). The study coordination center retained the master list and assigned treatments by phone.

domain_judgments.rationale: The open-label design permitted awareness of treatment, deviations affected 3%–11% of analyzed participants, and the modified intention-to-treat analysis excluded participants without measured outcomes, although directly observed mefloquine and corroborating per-protocol analyses reduce concern.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Deviations in the administration of the allocated treatment concerned 12 women (11% of the mITT population) and 8 women (3%) in the CNM and CM trials, respectively (Fig. 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was available for only 77%–80% of randomized women, and missingness was associated with HIV-diagnosis characteristics, so bias from missing outcome data cannot be excluded despite similar missing proportions across treatment groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Finally, 130/140 (92%) and 263/292 (90%) of women in the CNM and CM trials, respectively, were followed until delivery of a live or dead infant after 28 weeks of pregnancy (usual definition for stillbirth as opposed to spontaneous abortion), and 108 (77%) and 233 (80%), respectively, had the primary end point assessed.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was an objective microscopic measure applied consistently, with duplicate readings and blinded microscopists, making differential measurement unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For malaria diagnosis, thick and thin blood smears were stained with Giemsa and read by 2 independent microscopists, with conciliation of discrepancies by a third reader.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary endpoint and principal analyses were prespecified, but no prospective registration or analysis plan is reported and PCR-detected endpoints were added after a protocol amendment, leaving some potential for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Malarial infections detected by PCR in placental and peripheral blood at delivery were added as secondary end points after a protocol amendment.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because the primary endpoint was missing for approximately 20%–23% of randomized participants and missingness was associated with HIV-diagnosis characteristics. Additional concerns arise from incomplete reporting of sequence generation, the open-label design with treatment deviations, and lack of clear prospective analysis-plan documentation.
